thesis: New concepts earn value through distinct mechanisms and testable consequences rather than evocative names.
role: Develops bounded speculative architectures for access, time, identity and relevance.

ideas.statement: Access proximity and dependency time can be modeled without reproducing physical space or lived duration.
Branching histories need provenance; greater memory need not yield coherent understanding.
Multiple irreducible priorities and distributed control can be studied functionally without inferring experience.
Verbal possibility, coherence, computability, realizability, viability and experience require different arguments.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: An ecology of relevances preserves conflicts between energy, integrity and cooperation instead of one score.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: All proposed names label exercises, not discovered phenomena; conscious branches are an additional assumption.

audit.notes: Every unit read. Glossary treated as consolidation; all numerical worlds remain explicitly educational.
